layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—In order to clarify the mechanism for increased resistance to pitting in acid chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions by addition of Mo to Cr-Ni stainless steels, the anodic polarization curves, a.c. electrode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impedances, ellipsometric parameters and X-ray photo-electron spectra have been measured on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo-containing steels passivated in 1N HCl. The results showed that the presence of an adequate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amount of Cr is indispensable for the improvement of pitting resistance by the Mo addition. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive films of the Mo-containing steels were found to be composed of a complex oxyhydroxide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing Crª+ Fe³+, Ni²+, Moª+ and Cl- and showed a rather higher d.c. resistance in HCl solution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution. The thickness of the passive film increases with increase in Mo content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IT HAs long been known that additions of Mo to austenitic Cr-Ni stainless steels, to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marked degree, improve resistance to chloride pitting.1-1s The mechanism by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which the increased resistance is obtained is not well understood. According to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: literature, the following propositions have been made as to the effect of alloyed Mo:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) thickening of the passive films of the steels,14 (2) forming a heteropoly acid† film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is less readily hydrolysed and more readily polymerized,1⁵ (3) impeding the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adsorption of Cl- on to the surface of the steel by increasing the oxygen affinity of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel,8 and (4) forming an amorphous oxide film with a glassy structure.1º Each of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these effects is thought to be important and has to be taken into account in elucidating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mechanism for the improvement of pitting resistance by alloying with Mo. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition, however, the electrochemical behaviour of Mo in the potential region of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passivity for Mo-containing Cr-Ni steels must also be an important factor to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In previous work, it has been reported that alloyed Mo in Cr-Ni stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: causes the transpassive reaction in the potential range where the Mo-containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr-Ni steels passivate.17 A theoretical examination of thermodynamic data shows that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the product of the transpassive reaction of Mo depends on the pH of test solutions;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that is,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is formed in solutions with pH < ca. 3.5 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (or HMoO{) in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions with pH > ca. 3.5.18 Consequently, alloyed Mo in Cr-Ni stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will be retained in the passive films as a Mo(VI) oxide or dissolve into solutions as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: according to the pH of the solutions used when the Mo-containing Cr-Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels are polarized up to the potentials at which the steole pasivate.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can serve as a very effective pitting inhibitor, pitting of the Mo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing steels in neutral chloride solutions may be inhibited by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are formed by dissolution of Mo in the steels.17,19 In the case of acid chloride solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions are thermodynamically unstable, an increase in pitting resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the addition of Mo to the steels should be brought about by the improvement of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties of the passive films by Mo(VI) oxide present in the films.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The purpose of the present investigation is to clarify the origin of increased pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance with increasing Mo content in acid chloride solutions by examination of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition and characteristics of the passive films formed in these solutions. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this purpose, measurements of anodic polarization curves in HCl solution and, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some cases, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution, were performed on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: varying amounts of Mo, several pure components of the steels, and combinations of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the two alloying components. On the basis of the results of these polarization measure-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments, subsequent experiments were carried out to determine the critical composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at which Mo makes the steels highly resistant to pitting. Measurements of a.c.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impedance, ellipsometric parameters, and X-ray photo-electron spectra were then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conducted on the passive films formed on the surfaces of the Mo-containing Cr-Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels in order to investigate how the electrical properties, thickness, optical constants,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and chemical composition of the films change with the Mo content of the steels. On

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the basis of these experimental results, the role of alloyed Mo in the steels in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inhibition of pitting in acid chloride solutions is considered and discussed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Measurements of the anodic polarization curves in 1N HCl for the Mo-

layout_dets.text: containing Cr-Ni stainless steels with various compositions lead to the conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that additions of Mo improve the pitting resistance of the steels in the presence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr above a certain level which depends on the amount of Mo added. Mo decreases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr. Therefore, in order to clarify the mechanism for the improvement of the resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to pitting by alloyed Mo, it must be explained why the existence of Cr in steels is in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dispensable for deriving the beneficial effect of the Mo addition, and in particular,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: why the transpassive dissolution of Mo in the passive films is suppressed by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of Cr in the films of the steels. Since this type of improvement was thought to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be concerned with the composition and structure of the passive films, a consideration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was given at first to the chemical composition of the passive films formed on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 20Cr-25Ni-5Mo steel having a high corrosion resistance in 1N HCl.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: According to the XPS studies, the passive film of the 20Cr-25Ni-5Mo steel is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered to be an oxyhydroxide which contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cations. Among these ions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should play a very important role in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improving the corrosion resistance of the films. The corrosion resistance of the steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should increase when films which are mainly composed of Cr(III) oxyhydroxide and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo(VI) oxide are formed on the surfaces of the steels. It must be remembered, how-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, that Mo(VI) oxide, e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cannot form by itself a compact surface film having

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a good resistance to corrosion, as can be seen from Fig. 2, which shows that pure Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dissolves with a large rate producing an unprotective oxide film of

layout_dets.text: in the

layout_dets.text: potential range above

layout_dets.text: oxide. On the other hand, Cr(III)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxyhydroxide, e.g. CrOOH, can compose very compact surface films which are

layout_dets.text: mainly composed of a Cr(III) oxyhydroxide should result in increased resistance to

layout_dets.text: pitting as in the case of Fe-Cr alloys with high Cr contents.

layout_dets.text: alloys by XPS, it has been suggested that the passive films of the alloys with high Cr
